_comment: Coverage matrix for the shared Carve spec corpus (spec/tests/corpus/*.crv). Every NN-slug base category must appear in covered or skip; the coverage-matrix test fails otherwise so a new spec category forces a classify decision. covered = grammar parses every file in the category with no ERROR/MISSING node. skip = at least one file currently produces an ERROR/MISSING node; reason records the unmodeled construct (a grammar gap to surface, not to hack around). A skip key is a CATEGORY (NN-slug) or a single EXAMPLE (NN-slug-2) — use the example form when the rest of the category parses cleanly, so one gap does not drop assertion for its siblings. A key equal to a category name is read as the CATEGORY, so the first example of a category cannot be skipped on its own. REASONS: a ledger entry's `reason` may be `ref:<key>`, resolving against the top-level `reasons` map, so one grammar gap spanning a whole category states its explanation once. coverage-matrix gates it both ways - a ref with no entry fails, and a reasons entry nothing references fails, because a reason nobody points at is an excuse that outlived the gap it excused.

reasons.lone-cr-strands-a-column-probe: a lone carriage return still changes this document's tree. The scanner now treats all three spellings of `newline` as terminators, and 428 of 672 corpus documents that diverged before this do not any more, but these are the remainder: every one of them is a REFERENCE DEFINITION, an ATTRIBUTE BLOCK or a trailing block inside a list item - constructs whose probes read a column, and tree-sitter advances the row and resets the column on '\n' and on nothing else (`lib/src/lexer.c`), so a scanner-maintained base carries them and does not carry every probe that reads one. tree-sitter-carve#143. The same mechanism has one reachable shape outside the corpus: `comment_line` in grammar.js consumes its own terminator in the internal lexer, so a comment line ended by a lone '\r' strands the base for an indented construct below it.
reasons.fence-on-a-marker-line-builds-nothing: a code fence opened on a list MARKER line: the item closes with an EMPTY code block and the residue re-parses at document level when the body sits BELOW the item's content column (markup-carve/carve#646). This grammar builds no code_block for any of these, and MEASURED against it, the cause is NOT that the fence is committed to the item with no route out - it is that the fence never opens at all. `parse_backtick` refuses an opener when `has_extra_indent` is true, and on a marker line the fence sits past the line's own indent while the item's content column is only established by the marker itself, so `- ` + fence is read as inline verbatim. The heading marker and the colon fence carry the same column-0 guard and fail the same way on a marker line, while a block quote and a table - which do not - open there correctly. So the first half is a column question and the second half, closing the item at the boundary, is the container change; the fully-indented example (-3) needs only the first. Tracked in tree-sitter-carve#160.

skip.an-attribute-name-admits-no-colon-3: a table row whose trailing attribute block carries an INVALID name (`| a | b |{.a:b}` - a class may not contain a colon) parses to ERROR. The engines make the whole line a paragraph, because the block is not an attribute block at all; this grammar commits to the row on the pipes and has no route back. The category's other two examples parse cleanly, so only this one is skipped.
skip.a-blank-line-holds-spaces-and-tabs-and-n: a paragraph whose interior lines hold a single vertical tab, form feed, NEL (U+0085), LS (U+2028) or PS (U+2029) and nothing else parses to ERROR. PART 9 makes a line blank only when it holds spaces and tabs, so each of these is CONTENT and the paragraph runs through them; this grammar has no line-content route for a line whose only character is one of them. The category's other examples parse cleanly.
skip.trailing-whitespace-on-a-content-line-is: content lines ending in NBSP, ZWSP, BOM, U+2000 or a form feed parse to ERROR. Only the ASCII space and tab are dropped as trailing whitespace; every other spelling is content the renderer keeps, and this grammar's line-content rule does not admit them in that position. The category's other examples parse cleanly.
skip.a-quoted-attribute-value-stops-at-the-ne: a quoted attribute value carrying a newline (`{k="a` / `b"}`) parses to ERROR. The corpus pins it as literal text - the inline block does not span lines - but this grammar commits to an attribute block on the opening brace and has no route back to a paragraph when the value never closes on its line. Same class as an-attribute-name-admits-no-colon-3. The category's other examples parse cleanly.

an-unresolved-reference-image-takes-no-c.reason: `![a][nope]` + `^ cap` is one paragraph: the reference does not resolve, so the image is literal text and the `^` line is literal with it. Whether it resolves depends on the DEFINITIONS in the document, which a context-free grammar does not have - so the caption is built here and cannot be declined without a symbol table. The renderer decides correctly; highlighting a caption that the language declines is the cost.

a-frontmatter-opener-takes-exactly-one-s.reason: `---<SP><SP>yaml` is no longer read as a frontmatter opener - the opener's `[space]` slot takes exactly one space and the line is prose - but the `---` three lines below it, which the language turns into a thematic break, is folded into that prose instead. A thematic break does not interrupt an open paragraph in this grammar; `paragraph-interruption-3` records the same gap on a document with no frontmatter in it, and the two close together.

\"-\" + \"---\".reason: a `---` after a content-less marker errors; carve-js renders a paragraph then a thematic break (tree-sitter-carve#96)

The terminator is not the defect here, the unmodeled construct is, and the divergence goes away with it. Tracked in tree-sitter-carve#160.
